evidence.claim: About 1 in 5 people in Michigan have a disability; transportation resources are not always available to them.
More than 128,000 Detroiters, roughly one in five residents, have at least one disability.
Uber and other rideshare programs are not required by federal law to be accessible.

Riders and advocates complained for years about missed pickups, long waits and poor customer service; in 2022 riders urged council to reject a ~$50M Transdev contract; in 2023, facing a shutdown, the mayor awarded short-term contracts to four local companies.
The federal government warned Detroit it was violating federal law by failing to fully fund paratransit.
evidence.publisher: CBS News Detroit (citing The Detroit News)

evidence.claim: Blind Detroit riders told the Department of Justice about chronically late drivers who left them in the cold or dropped them at the wrong location, and said officials ignored their concerns for years.

DDOT launched 'DDOT Now' same-day paratransit in June 2025: trips bookable about one hour ahead, $2.50 fare, same service area; DDOT says on-time performance is at least 98% for each provider and publishes a performance dashboard.
evidence.publisher: Mass Transit Magazine / City of Detroit; WDET
evidence.use: fairness: things are improving, and agency data is self-reported

evidence.claim: Detroit paratransit ridership nearly doubled, according to DDOT (reported August 2025).

A February 18, 2026 coalition letter to Mayor Mary Sheffield (including Transportation Riders United and the Greater Detroit Agency for the Blind & Visually Impaired) called for borderless paratransit so riders don't have to transfer at the city limit.

In the RTA region, 85% of trips on existing transit services begin and end within a single county; riders face gaps in opt-out communities and long waits where providers meet, and want standardized eligibility.
evidence.publisher: Regional Transit Authority of Southeast Michigan, Mobility 4 All (2025)

evidence.claim: SMART announced new scheduling software with push notifications and real-time tracking; paratransit riders can manage trips through an app (January 2026).
evidence.use: competitive landscape: agency apps manage trips, but don't give riders an independent record across providers

evidence.claim: A Farmington Hills man who uses a powered wheelchair said repeated failures of his insurance-covered medical transportation caused him to miss nearly a dozen doctor's appointments in 2026: last-minute cancellations, vans that couldn't fit his chair, and a return ride that never came. The ride company pointed to its third-party providers and his insurer; the insurer cited privacy rules.

Michigan's Office of the Auditor General has an in-progress audit of Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation; NEMT expenditures totaled $160.5M from Oct 1, 2024 to Mar 31, 2026; estimated release late 2026.
evidence.publisher: Michigan Office of the Auditor General

evidence.claim: A prior audit by Michigan's Office of the Auditor General found the state's Medicaid non-emergency transportation system not effective.
In a 2025 study of rural Iosco County, 26% of respondents experienced care disruptions related to transportation and 9.5% had medical care delayed or cancelled.
Patients and advocates say Medicaid ride problems often go unreported or complaints are ignored.
DDOT driver pay started at $19/hour vs. $27/hour at SMART, contributing to high turnover (2025).
evidence.publisher: Transportation Riders United, 2025 Detroit Transit Policy Platform

evidence.claim: 49 CFR 37.131(f) prohibits capacity constraints in ADA paratransit, including operational patterns with substantial numbers of significantly untimely pickups, trip denials or missed trips, and trips with excessive trip lengths. The regulations do not define 'substantial.'
Excessive telephone hold times for reserving trips are among the operational practices treated as capacity constraints.

The FTA Civil Rights Complaint Form includes a section for paratransit on-time performance complaints and asks for specific dates and times; FTA encourages riders to first file with their local transit agency.
